# Overview {.unnumbered}

_One 2-hour session_

:::{.callout-note title="Learning Goals" collapse="false"}
After this lesson, you should be able to:

* Explain why the cause of missingness in a dataset matters
* Explain the differences between data MCAR, MAR, and MNAR
* Describe some R packages for exploring and handling missing data
* Visualize missing data to identify patterns
* Explain what complete- and available-case analysis are
* Explain what single and multiple imputation are
* Use the mice package to perform multiple imputation on a dataset
* Explain what censoring means for a dataset
* Explain the differences between left-, right-, and interval-censored data
* Explain why substitution is inappropriate for censored data
* Describe several appropriate ways to work with censored data
* Visualize censored data with ECDF and probability plots
* Use the NADA package to compute statistics that account for censored data
:::

This workshop introduces a variety of statistical methods and models to account
for missing or censored measurements in datasets. We’ll begin by reviewing
different types of missingness and censorship. We’ll then discuss specific
models and strategies for imputation and estimation, when they’re appropriate,
and when they break down. Extra emphasis will be given to techniques for
working with nondetect (left-censored) measurements.
